items_missed: Never asked the customer's name or used it at any point in the call ('Hi, this is Jules. How can I help you today?' straight into logistics)
No agenda statement setting expectations for the call (what will be covered, how long it takes) or a 'sound good?' confirmation
Never asked home size (bedrooms/sq ft) — quoted the time estimate assuming 'a one bedroom apartment' without the customer ever stating or confirming that
No probe for additional rooms (garage, storage unit, balcony), packing needs, box count, storage stops, additional stops, or moving stressors
Destination zip code never captured (only the street address for 8509 Shelton Chalton Drive, Plano was given — origin zip 75201 was captured)
No 'pricing is super simple' framing beyond 'let me quickly discuss the pricing'
No mention of No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000 for accidental damage)
No mention of Meet Your Mover (photo/info email before the move)
No mention of On-Time Guarantee (discounting if the arrival window is missed) — relevant here since an arrival window was explicitly negotiated
'No hidden fees' pitch was a generic 'we do not charge any additional fees' rather than the itemized no-credit-card-fee / no-transportation-fee / no-fuel-surcharge / no-assembly-fee list
Estimate never explained variables like stairs/elevator impact, walk distance, drive time between Dallas and Plano, or used an equivalents comparison (e.g. school bus reference)
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no mention that pre-move prep/consolidation (toys, garden tools, loose drawer items, wall photos) or taking a carload shortens the move and lowers the bill
Never explicitly said 'no deposit required' — only stated payment is due after the move is completed
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?' before ending the call
No office hours or how-to-reach-us info given
Insurance was named in the included-fees list but never explained (no No Worries $2,000 detail or 60¢/lb baseline)
No rapport-building, humor, or empathy language — call stayed fully transactional start to finish
top_strength: Jules ran the clock explanation cleanly and completely (start-on-arrival, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute proration, plus a 'do you have any questions about that?' sense-check), and proactively adjusted the arrival window to 1-3 PM on the fly to line up with the customer's freight elevator reservation.
coaching_note: Jules quoted the move assuming 'a one bedroom apartment' without ever asking how many bedrooms or the home's size — confirm home size (and the destination zip) before quoting, and add the Save Your Ass prep speech plus the No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee differentiators, none of which were mentioned on this call.
phone_presence_notes: Jules was polite and responsive (readily adjusted the arrival window for the elevator, used affirmations like 'Awesome' and 'Great') but never used the customer's name and kept the call fully task-focused with no rapport or empathy language beyond the transaction.
